newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia opposition urges steel industry plan.
newsitem.headline: Australia opposition urges steel industry plan.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition on Tuesday urged the government and steel industry to urgently draft a new plan to bolster the industry after The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said it would scale back its steel operations.
Opposition industry spokesman Simon Crean said Australia could not afford to simply be a quarry for the world and must develop downstream manufacturing capacity.
"Australia can't be content to just being an iron ore supplier to our trading partners," he told Reuters.
"The government's just got to get involved. It's got to convene urgent talks with BHP to develop a steel plan," Crean said.
Crean said the government, unions and industry must pull together to draft an industry strategy for the next 10 to 15 years, focussing on value-added production.
He accused Prime Minister John Howard of abandoning the industry, "because the prime minister sees Australia as the world's quarry".
BHP said it would phase out steelmaking at its major Newcastle plant, north of Sydney, by the end of 1999 and close its Geelong rod mill, in Victoria, and Sydney wire mill in 1999.
Based on a review of domestic and international steel operations, BHP said it would disband its international steel division and restructure BHP Steel around four divisions.
The company said it would shed up to 2,500 jobs with the closure of raw steel making at Newcastle, a traditional industrial centre named after the English industrial city.
Crean said he was disappointed BHP, Australia's largest listed company, had acted before a parliamentary committee had completed a review of the steel industry.
"I am disappointed that BHP has taken the decision, given that the committee has not yet concluded its hearings, let alone handed down their findings," he said.
